rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes `C[row * N + col] = 0.0f` to `C[row / N + col] = 0.0f` in the else branch (col > row). With N=4096 and row ∈ [0, 4095], `row / N = 0` always (integer division). So mutated writes go to C[col] instead of C[row*N+col]. However: (1) All these writes are 0.0f. (2) C is initialized to zeros via torch::zeros. (3) The written positions C[col] for col ∈ [1, 4095] correspond to upper triangular positions (0, col) which should be 0. (4) Lower triangular computations in the if-branch are unaffected. Therefore, despite writing to different memory locations, the final output matrix is identical.
rounds.survival_reason: The else branch executes only for upper triangular positions (col > row), where the output should always be zero. The original code writes 0.0f to C[row*N+col], the mutated code writes 0.0f to C[row/N+col]=C[col]. Since C is pre-initialized to all zeros, writing zeros to different upper-triangular locations produces the same final result. The mutation essentially becomes a redundant write to already-zero memory. The lower triangular computations in the if-branch (col <= row) are completely unaffected by this mutation. No value pattern can expose a difference because the mutation only affects which zero-valued positions receive explicit zero-writes, not the computed values.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation only changes which memory addresses receive explicit zero writes in the upper triangular region. Since the output is pre-initialized to zeros and all affected writes are zeros, no input values can produce a distinguishable output. The mutation is semantically equivalent to the original under all possible input values.
rounds.recommendations: This mutation reveals a testing blind spot: mutations that change memory write locations but not values can survive when the written value matches initialization. Consider adding static analysis to detect when a mutation affects write addresses in branches that only write constant values matching tensor initialization, flagging such mutations as likely equivalent.
